messages:
Emma (Support): Hey team — customer 'Acme Health' reporting intermittent 401s and UI hangs on 'Create API Key' flow. Happened behind corporate proxy + macOS Safari (user reported iOS Safari too). Request ID they provided: req_0a1b2c3d. They can repro ~50% of attempts. Asking for exact repro capture steps (HAR + console) and a safe curl to reproduce server-side.

Raj (SRE): Thanks. Quick checklist: 1) ask for full request-id headers + exact user-agent string 2) ask whether they're on a proxy w/ TLS interception 3) get timestamp window for failures (UTC). If they can reproduce, tell them to capture HAR + console and redact tokens.

Emma (Support): Got UA: "Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_4 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/16.4 Mobile/15E148 Safari/605.1.15". They say corporate proxy with certificate pinning might be off. Failure times: 2026-03-16T19:02:11Z — 19:07:30Z.

Tyler (DevEx): For macOS Safari (desktop) and iOS Safari flow — recommended approaches: short, pick one that matches their environment. Include both so we can cover regulated customers.

Tyler (DevEx): macOS Safari (when they can reproduce on the laptop):
1) Open Safari > Preferences > Advanced > enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar"
2) Reproduce the issue with the DevTools open: Develop > Show Web Inspector (Cmd+Opt+I)
3) In Web Inspector, select Network tab, clear, then reproduce the flow.
4) Right-click any request > Export HAR (or Use the Export button) — if export isn't available, copy the network log as HAR-compatible JSON.
5) Console tab: copy errors, console.log, and network stack traces.
6) IMPORTANT: redact Authorization / session cookies before upload. Replace with <REDACTED_AUTH>.

Tyler (DevEx): iOS Safari (device attached to mac):
1) Connect iPhone to mac via USB. On the iPhone: Settings > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector = ON.
2) On mac Safari Develop menu > select the connected device > open the page.
3) Perform the failing action while Network and Console are visible in the remote inspector.
4) Export as HAR from the remote inspector or use the right-click export on requests. If the environment blocks, use a local proxy (see below).

Tyler (DevEx): If they cannot attach device or have corporate proxy that prevents Web Inspector exports, use a proxy capture: Charles, Fiddler Everywhere, or mitmproxy. Steps (high level):
- Install and run the proxy, trust CA on device and mac.
- Reproduce the failure while capture is running.
- Save the session as HAR or Charles session.
- Mask tokens: use the proxy's replace rule to scrub Authorization before exporting if possible.

Raj (SRE): For server-side repro via curl, ask them to run this locally (redact token first):

```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"test-key"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.chat/v1/keys"
```

Raj (SRE): If curl returns 401, include full verbose output, response headers, and server timestamp. If curl succeeds but browser fails consistently, that's a client-side issue (CORS, cookie, redirect).

Maria (Product): Two UI-specific checks we want captured in console HAR: 1) SSO redirect chain (look for 302 -> postMessage or form POST), 2) any Mixed Content or blocked cookie warnings. Please annotate which click leads to the failure.

Emma (Support): Customer is also seeing repeated 429s after failure for ~30s. Could be retry loop from client. Asking them to preserve sequence of events in HAR (don't clear timeline).

Tyler (DevEx): Additional useful logs to include: network.requestWillBeSent/responseReceived entries (if using Chrome), the full request/response headers for the failed request, and any stacktrace in console. If they can, grab a browser performance trace (not required).

Emma (Support): We also need system network info: OS version, browser version, corporate VPN/proxy name, and whether client uses a custom PAC file.

Raj (SRE): If they can't share HAR publicly, have them use our secure upload helper. support-bot will create a one-time upload link and auto-delete after 7 days. Also ask for the server-side request-id header (we log x-rw-reqid in our backend).

support-bot: Hi — I created a secure upload for Acme Health: https://files.redwood.ai/upload/xxxx-unique-link (expires in 7 days). Please upload the HAR + console.txt + curl-output.txt. Use the customer email acme+support@acme.example for the upload metadata.

Emma (Support): Pasting a sample redaction checklist to send to customer: remove Authorization header value, remove any full API keys, remove PII in request bodies (names/emails), and mark sensitive files with [REDACTED] in the filename.

Tyler (DevEx): If the customer is stuck exporting HAR from Safari (it sometimes lacks a direct export): open Chrome, reproduce the failing flow there (set UA to Safari if needed) and export HAR from Chrome DevTools (Network > Save as HAR). Often easier for capture.

Emma (Support): Customer uploaded a 12MB file to the secure link. devtools-bot — can you fetch/sanitize and attach the trimmed HAR?

devtools-bot: Fetched upload: acme-2512345678.har (12MB). Running automated scrub: removed Authorization headers and replaced cookie values with <REDACTED>. Trimmed duplicate static assets; output: acme-2512345678-scrubbed.har (3.4MB). Attached to thread.

Raj (SRE): Thanks — I'll take a look at the scrubbed HAR around req_0a1b2c3d. Next steps: correlate x-rw-reqid with backend logs between 2026-03-16T19:02:11Z and 19:07:30Z and check for 401 reasons (expired token vs. auth-service misrouting).

Maria (Product): If we confirm proxy rewriting or missing SameSite cookies, we'll add recommended mitigation notes for the KB article.

Emma (Support): Great. I'll update the customer with the secure link + curl snippet and ask them to run the verbose curl and paste the output into the upload. Closing initial triage for now — will follow up with backend correlation results. :thumbsup:
